READ-ONLY REVIEW of C:\civicfix\apps\web\src\app\worker\dashboard\page.tsx (162 lines). No files edited. VERDICT: all three parts of the claim are CONFIRMED.

(1) 'Decline' only when status === 'ASSIGNED' — CONFIRMED.
The only render of the Decline button is inside the ASSIGNED guard at page.tsx:93-105:
  93  {status === 'ASSIGNED' && (
  94    <>
  95      <Button onClick={() => act.mutate({ id: c.id, status: 'ACCEPTED', note })}>Accept</Button>
  98      <Button variant="secondary"
  100       onClick={() => act.mutate({ id: c.id, status: 'UNDER_REVIEW', note })}>
  102        Decline
No other branch (ACCEPTED:106-110, ON_HOLD:111-115, IN_PROGRESS:116-123) renders a Decline button. Note the 'Decline' action mutates status to 'UNDER_REVIEW', not to a declined/rejected status (page.tsx:100).

(2) 'Mark complete' gated behind an uploaded 'AFTER' photo for that task — CONFIRMED (with a client-side-only caveat).
  69  const hasAfter = (uploads[c.id] ?? []).includes('AFTER');
 116  {status === 'IN_PROGRESS' && (
 117    <Button
 118      disabled={!hasAfter}
 119      onClick={() => act.mutate({ id: c.id, status: 'RESOLVED', note })}>
 121      Mark complete
The gate is per-task (keyed by c.id in the uploads record, page.tsx:22-33) and is populated only by this session's uploads — upload mutation's onSuccess at page.tsx:59 calls addKind(prev, input.id, input.kind) (addKind defined page.tsx:24-27), with the After-photo input posting kind: 'AFTER' at page.tsx:145. UI hint confirming intent at page.tsx:151-155 ('Upload an after photo to mark this task complete.'). CAVEAT: `uploads` is React useState (page.tsx:33), not server-derived — so the button is disabled purely on client-side evidence collected in this browser session; a previously uploaded AFTER photo (or one uploaded in another session) does not re-enable it after reload, and nothing here proves server-side enforcement.
